# isScalar

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a scalar.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isScalar() — Checks whether a value is a scalar. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isScalar(value: unknown): value is string | number | boolean | symbol | bigint;
```

A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a scalar; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `string | number | boolean | symbol | bigint` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isScalar("abc"); // => true
isScalar(1); // => true
isScalar(true); // => true
isScalar(10n); // => true
isScalar({}); // => false
isScalar([]); // => false
isScalar(null); // => false
```
